title: TimesNet: Temporal 2D-Variation Modeling for General Time Series Analysis
grouping: Three stages without containers: an axis plot of the raw series at the left with nested brackets 'Period 1/2/3' above it; dashed arrows from each bracket to a diagonal staircase of period stacks in the middle; hollow block arrows to three slanted 2-D planes at the right. A legend in the lower-left explains the circles and the two arrow colours.
shapes_depth: The series is a grey line on a Value/Time axis. In the middle each period's segments are drawn as offset copies of the grey curve on alternating pale blue and pale pink rectangles; black hollow circles mark time points at the same phase and dashed lines join them across copies. Dark blue arrows trace the interperiod variation along a copy, dark red curved arrows the intraperiod variation across copies. The right-hand 2-D planes are white parallelograms in perspective containing short black curve fragments, with a long blue arrow along one edge and a red arrow along the other; finer periods give more, narrower cells.
proposed_highlight: The paper's key idea (two kinds of variation) owns the only two saturated colours, blue and red, used identically on the curve overlays, the 2-D planes' axes and the legend.
lesson: Explain a 1-D-to-2-D reshape by cutting the drawn series into period segments stacked as offset copies with same-phase points joined, and give the two resulting axes their own colours (blue across periods, red within) on both the curves and the final 2-D planes.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF header (Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
